ordered.title: Why DPFs Fail
ordered.description: Understanding the root cause helps you prevent future issues.

cards.title: 🚗 Short journeys
cards.text: DPF can't regenerate because exhaust doesn't get hot enough. The filter never reaches 600°C+ to burn off soot.
cards.fullText: 🚗 Short journeys DPF can't regenerate because exhaust doesn't get hot enough. The filter never reaches 600°C+ to burn off soot. ✔ Prevention: Regular longer journeys (40mph+ for 20 mins)

cards.title: 🔧 Faulty EGR valve
cards.text: EGR recirculates exhaust gases — adds soot to DPF, accelerating clogging.
cards.fullText: 🔧 Faulty EGR valve EGR recirculates exhaust gases — adds soot to DPF, accelerating clogging. ✔ Prevention: Regular maintenance, EGR cleaning

cards.title: 💉 Faulty injectors
cards.text: Over-fuelling creates more soot, clogging the DPF faster.
cards.fullText: 💉 Faulty injectors Over-fuelling creates more soot, clogging the DPF faster. ✔ Prevention: Regular maintenance, injector cleaning

cards.title: 🛢️ Oil ash accumulation
cards.text: Oil ash builds up over time — can't be regenerated away. Requires professional cleaning.
cards.fullText: 🛢️ Oil ash accumulation Oil ash builds up over time — can't be regenerated away. Requires professional cleaning. ✔ Prevention: Regular DPF cleaning (every 30,000–40,000 miles)

cards.title: 📡 Faulty sensors
cards.text: Pressure/temperature sensors fail — ECU doesn't know when to regenerate.
cards.fullText: 📡 Faulty sensors Pressure/temperature sensors fail — ECU doesn't know when to regenerate. ✔ Prevention: Regular diagnostics, faulty sensor replacement

cards.title: ⛽ Low engine oil level
cards.text: Over-filling or low oil can cause DPF issues. Use the correct oil spec.
cards.fullText: ⛽ Low engine oil level Over-filling or low oil can cause DPF issues. Use the correct oil spec. ✔ Prevention: Regular oil checks, correct oil spec (ACEA C1/C2/C3)

blocks.text: 💡 Why short journeys cause DPF problems: For the DPF to regenerate, the exhaust must reach 600°C+ . This requires sustained driving at 40mph+ for 15-20 minutes . If you only do short journeys, the DPF never gets hot enough — soot accumulates and the DPF clogs.

ordered.title: 10 Questions to Ask Before DPF Service
ordered.description: Asking the right questions can save you hundreds and prevent unnecessary replacement. Here's a checklist specific to DPF issues.

blocks.text: 1. Is cleaning possible or do I need replacement?
In most cases, cleaning resolves the issue. Replacement is only needed if cracked, melted, or severely damaged.
2. What's included in the cleaning price?
Get a full written breakdown: removal, cleaning, refitting, testing, and diagnostic reset.
3. What cleaning method do you use?
Off-car cleaning (best), forced regeneration (mild issues), or chemical (less effective).
4. What's the condition of my DPF?
Ask for an inspection report. Is it clogged with soot, ash, or physically damaged?
5. What warranty do you offer on the cleaning?
Typical warranty is 6–12 months on the cleaning work. Get it in writing.
6. What's the root cause of the DPF issue?
Short journeys, faulty EGR, faulty injectors, or something else? Address the root cause.
7. What's the timeline from booking to completion?
Off-car cleaning: 1-2 days. Forced regeneration: a few hours. Replacement: 2-3 days.
8. Is there any diagnostic work included?
Ask if fault code reading and DPF pressure measurement are included in the price.
9. Do you have experience with my vehicle/engine type?
Some engines have known DPF issues. Ask about their experience.
10. Can you provide a written quote?
Get everything in writing: scope of work, cost, timeline, and warranty terms.

Yes - a clean DPF restores performance. You'll notice restored power, improved fuel economy, smoother engine running, no DPF warning light, and no smoke.

mainEntity.name: How long does a DPF last-

acceptedAnswer.text: A DPF should last 100,000+ miles with regular maintenance. However, DPFs can fail earlier due to short journeys, faulty components, or poor maintenance.
Any major mechanical work, including DPF replacement, should be declared to your insurer. DPF removal (illegal) will void your insurance.
